basketMaterials.name: Standard PTFE Non-Stick Coated Steel Basket (15–25 µm Fluoropolymer)
basketMaterials.toxicGasOutgassingRisk: Moderate at 200°C; High during empty dry preheating (>230°C)
basketMaterials.avianHazardLevel: High Risk (Fatal polymer fume fever in pet birds if overheated)
basketMaterials.description: The standard non-stick basket fitted to the vast majority of consumer air fryers. Employs a multi-coat fluoropolymer finish that is non-reactive at normal cooking temperatures with food moisture, but susceptible to radiant overheating, thermal micro-cracking, and ultrafine fluorocarbon aerosolization during empty dry preheating.

basketMaterials.name: Inorganic Ceramic Sol-Gel Coated Basket (PTFE / PFAS-Free)
basketMaterials.coatingType: Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) & Titanium Dioxide Nano-Composite Sol-Gel
basketMaterials.avianHazardLevel: Safe (Completely benign to pet birds; no fluorinated gases)
basketMaterials.description: Modern non-toxic alternative employing a spray-applied inorganic silica sol-gel ceramic matrix cured at high temperatures. Totally immune to fluoropolymer thermal breakdown and PTFE gas release even at temperatures up to 450°C (842°F), though non-stick release properties degrade more rapidly over repeated abrasive dishwasher cycles.

basketMaterials.name: 304 Food-Grade Stainless Steel Perforated Basket & Wire Rack (Uncoated)
basketMaterials.coatingType: Bare Passivated Chromium-Nickel Steel (18/8 Cr-Ni, No Coating)
basketMaterials.avianHazardLevel: Completely Safe (Zero outgassing at any residential temperature)
basketMaterials.description: Heavy-duty commercial and high-end consumer option featuring unpainted, uncoated 304 stainless steel. Totally impervious to thermal degradation, dry-run preheat fires, or mechanical scouring. Eliminates all fluoropolymer and microplastic concerns, though requires light oil seasoning to prevent protein sticking.

basketMaterials.name: Borosilicate / Tempered Glass Cooking Chamber (Transparent Drawer)
basketMaterials.baseSubstrate: Borosilicate 3.3 Glass with 304 Stainless Trivet Insert
basketMaterials.avianHazardLevel: Completely Safe (Zero airborne particulate or chemical migration)
basketMaterials.description: Premium panoramic air fryer basket crafted from heavy molded thermal borosilicate glass. Offers complete optical monitoring of food browning, zero chemical outgassing, and 100% resistance to fat burn-on staining, with the single engineering constraint of avoiding sudden cold water thermal shock while hot (ΔT > 120°C).

basketMaterials.name: Degraded / Severely Flaking PTFE Basket (Compromised Non-Stick)
basketMaterials.coatingType: Fragmented & Delaminating PTFE with Exposed Primer & Bare Aluminum
basketMaterials.toxicGasOutgassingRisk: Severe (High-velocity forced convection peels micro-flakes into air & food)
basketMaterials.avianHazardLevel: Critical / Lethal (Rapid emission of fluorocarbon breakdown aerosols)
basketMaterials.description: Severely degraded basket where repeated metal utensil scouring, aerosol spray varnish, and overheating have fractured the fluoropolymer matrix. High-velocity 3,000 RPM convection air currents rip microscopic PTFE fragments (100 nm to 50 µm) directly from peeling basket margins into the swirling thermal vortex, contaminating food and kitchen air.

preheatAndLoadConditions.name: Full Food Load (Chicken, Vegetables, Fries as Thermal Heat Sink)
preheatAndLoadConditions.description: Food moisture evaporation (latent heat of vaporization, 2260 kJ/kg) dynamically buffers basket surface temperature, keeping metal coating significantly cooler than the surrounding convective air stream.

preheatAndLoadConditions.name: Light Snack / Single Serving (Sparse Thermal Mass)
preheatAndLoadConditions.description: A small handful of food covers less than 30% of basket surface area, leaving wide expanses of coated wire exposed to direct radiant heating from overhead elements.

preheatAndLoadConditions.name: Empty Dry-Run Preheat (No Food / Direct Radiant Flux)
preheatAndLoadConditions.description: Without food to absorb thermal energy, radiant flux from the glowing heating element (located just 3–5 cm above the basket) superheats the dark PTFE coating, causing surface hot-spots 30°C–50°C higher than the thermostat sensor reading.

preheatAndLoadConditions.name: Extended Empty Dry-Run (>10 min Dry Preheat / Burn-Off Cycle)
preheatAndLoadConditions.description: Severe thermal stress condition often initiated by consumers attempting to 'burn off factory odors'. Chamber temperature rapidly overshoots thermostat set points, triggering acute PTFE pyrolysis and dense micro-plume formation.

temperatureSettings.name: 160°C (320°F) – Gentle Roast / Dehydrate
temperatureSettings.description: Sub-pyrolysis operating temperature. Fluoropolymer bonds remain intact; minimal thermal outgassing occurs even in empty baskets.

temperatureSettings.name: 180°C (356°F) – Standard Baking / Reheating
temperatureSettings.description: Normal cooking temperature. Safe with food present; minor low-molecular-weight fluoropolymer outgassing occurs if preheated empty for prolonged periods.

temperatureSettings.name: 200°C (392°F) – Standard Crisp & Air Fry
temperatureSettings.description: Baseline air fry temperature. Sits right at the thermal decomposition threshold for lower-grade fluoropolymer additives. Radiant hot spots during preheat cross 220°C.

temperatureSettings.name: 220°C (428°F) – Max Crisp / French Fry Finish
temperatureSettings.description: Maximum factory setting on modern air fryers. Pushes PTFE coating to its continuous safe operating limit. Empty basket radiant surface temperatures can hit 250°C–260°C.

temperatureSettings.name: 240°C (464°F) – Thermostat Drift / Over-Temp Hotspot
temperatureSettings.description: Severe overheating scenario caused by uncalibrated thermostat sensors, blocked exhaust vents, or high-radiance heating element proximity. Active thermal decomposition of PTFE into toxic fluorocarbon gases.

coatingWearStates.name: Pristine / Factory New (Zero Scratches)
coatingWearStates.description: Uniform mirror-finish fluoropolymer film with 100% surface cohesion. Minimal exposed edges for mechanical peeling.

coatingWearStates.name: Micro-Scratched (Fork Tines & Abrasive Sponge Marks)
coatingWearStates.description: Linear micro-grooves breach the outer clear coat, exposing underlying primer layer. Convection air currents create microscopic boundary turbulence along furrow edges.

coatingWearStates.name: Heavily Abraded (Exposed Metal Margins on Wire Mesh)
coatingWearStates.description: Widespread coating wear on high-friction basket corners and mesh intersections. Exposed base metal allows grease to seep beneath adjacent coating edges, undermining adhesion.

coatingWearStates.name: Active Delamination & Blistering (Peeling Flakes)
coatingWearStates.description: Blistered and lifting coating flaps. High-velocity 3,000 RPM airflow tears micro-particles (1 to 50 microns) directly into the swirling hot air stream, contaminating both food and indoor air.

oilSprayTypes.name: Dry / No Added Cooking Fat
oilSprayTypes.description: Clean convection air stream without lipid degradation products.

oilSprayTypes.name: High-Smoke Point Liquid Oil (Avocado / High-Oleic Sunflower Brushed)
oilSprayTypes.description: Pure triglyceride oil without emulsifiers. Forms a light sacrificial thermal boundary layer that protects food without chemically degrading the fluoropolymer basket.

oilSprayTypes.name: Commercial Aerosol Cooking Spray (Lecithin + Isobutane Propellant)
oilSprayTypes.description: Pressurized cooking spray cans contain soy lecithin emulsifiers and chemical propellants. At air fryer temperatures above 175°C, lecithin rapidly polymerizes into an insoluble, gummy amber varnish that chemically bonds to PTFE. Removing this varnish requires aggressive scrubbing, which rips the non-stick coating off the metal.

ventilationStates.name: High-CFM Ducted Range Hood Exhausting Outdoors (300+ CFM)
ventilationStates.description: Overhead range hood captures and vents thermal convective exhaust directly outside, preventing accumulation of aerosolized ultrafine particles in household breathing zones.

ventilationStates.name: Passive Kitchen Window Ajar (Cross-Ventilation)
ventilationStates.description: Partial dilution ventilation. Drops ambient particulate concentration over 30–45 minutes, but localized breathing-zone plumes remain elevated near the countertop.

ventilationStates.name: Enclosed / Windowless Kitchen (Zero Active Ventilation)
ventilationStates.description: Critical exposure scenario. Convection fan exhaust discharges directly into living space air. Ultrafine particles and fluorinated vapors reach peak equilibrium concentrations within 10 minutes and linger for hours.
